1	# Error taxonomy — 13 codes
2	
3	Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.
4	
5	| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
8	| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
9	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
10	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
11	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
12	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
13	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
14	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
15	| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
16	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
17	| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
18	| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
19	| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |
20	
21	**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
22	- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
23	- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.
24	
25	**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
26

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

162	|---|---|---|

165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

1	import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart';

3	part 'failure.freezed.dart';
4	
5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

15	/// (Code Map). A raw `Box<Map>`, not a generated `HiveObject`/
16	/// `TypeAdapter` (Design Notes: avoids adapter codegen) — spec-4-1's
17	/// `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` is this box's first reader
18	/// (`create()`'s own writes were, until then, never read back by
19	/// anything).

22	/// Registers the `entries` feature into the project's single `get_it`
23	/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `features/account/account_injection.dart`'s
24	/// pattern. Called from `setupCoreDependencies()` right after
25	/// `Hive.initFlutter()` (Code Map), which must already have run by the
26	/// time this opens its box.
27	Future<void> registerEntriesFeature() async {
28	  final entriesBox = await Hive.openBox<Map>(entriesBoxName);
29	  sl.registerSingleton<Box<Map>>(entriesBox);
30	
31	  sl.registerLazySingleton<EntriesRemoteDataSource>(
32	    () => EntriesRemoteDataSource(sl<ApiClient>()),
33	  );

35	  sl.registerLazySingleton<EntriesRepository>(
36	    () => EntriesRepositoryImpl(
37	      remoteDataSource: sl<EntriesRemoteDataSource>(),
38	      entriesBox: sl<Box<Map>>(),
39	    ),

42	  // spec-4-2 — one shared tracker for all three capture cubits

44	  // pending write started from any capture cubit is visible to the other
45	  // regardless of which "+" tap created it (Design Notes).
46	  sl.registerLazySingleton<PendingEntryWriteTracker>(
47	    () => PendingEntryWriteTrackerImpl(repository: sl<EntriesRepository>()),
48	    dispose: (tracker) => tracker.dispose(),

50

52	  // (Code Map/Boundaries), like `AccountSettingsCubit`: long-lived, so

56	    () => MeusRegistrosCubit(

64	  // mirroring `MeusRegistrosCubit` immediately above: long-lived, so

28	  ///
29	  /// spec-5-2 — [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] are forwarded to
30	  /// `entries-list` as its own `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` query
31	  /// parameters (`EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`'s own doc), each only
32	  /// when non-null; combining more than one narrows with AND logic (the
33	  /// backend's own semantics, RF06 Acceptance Criteria) — this repository
34	  /// does no client-side filtering/joining of its own (AD-9).
35	  ///
36	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
37	  /// falls back to a full dump of the `entries` Hive box, sorted
38	  /// `occurredAt` desc, with `EntriesPage.nextCursor: null` (Boundaries) —
39	  /// every *other* [Failure] (e.g. [Failure.authExpired]) propagates as
40	  /// `Left`, unmapped (RNF09). That fallback (`cursor == null` only) stays
41	  /// filter-oblivious regardless of [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] — AD-9:
42	  /// the cache is never locally filtered, so an offline first page always
43	  /// renders the full cached list even with filters active.
44	  ///
45	  /// A successful page persists every item to the `entries` Hive box
46	  /// *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
47	  /// [create] already uses.
48	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({
49	    String? cursor,
50	    int limit = 20,
51	    EntrySource? source,
52	    DateTime? dateFrom,
53	    DateTime? dateTo,
54	  });
55	
56	  /// spec-4-4 (RF07) — calls `entries-get` (`ApiClient.get`, via
57	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [id] as the one path parameter, then
58	  /// persists the fetched entry to the `entries` Hive box (`put`) *before*
59	  /// returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
60	  /// [create]/[list] already use. AD-11 keeps this port create+read-only,
61	  /// not count-capped — [search] (spec-5-1) added a fourth method without
62	  /// contradicting that.
63	  ///
64	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
65	  /// falls back to `entriesBox.get(id)` if present; a cache miss propagates
66	  /// the original failure unchanged (no synthesized not-found — that
67	  /// distinction belongs to whichever `Failure` the backend/network
68	  /// actually produced). Every *other* [Failure] — including
69	  /// [Failure.notFound] for an id that never existed or belongs to another
70	  /// user — is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09); RNF04 (identical
71	  /// treatment for both causes) is the caller's own rendering job, never
72	  /// this repository's.
73	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
74	
75	  /// spec-5-1 — calls `entries-search` (`ApiClient.get`, via
76	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [query] as the one `q` query
77	  /// parameter (no `limit`/`cursor` — Boundaries). [query] is always
78	  /// already a non-empty, pre-trimmed string by the time it reaches this
79	  /// method — `EntriesSearchCubit` owns that guarantee, never this
80	  /// repository.
81	  ///
82	  /// spec-5-3 — [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] are forwarded to
83	  /// `entries-search` as its own `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` query
84	  /// parameters, each only when non-null — same AND-narrowing convention
85	  /// [list]'s own doc already gives, now carried by `EntriesSearchCubit`'s
86	  /// own filter fields (`updateFilters()`) instead of `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s
87	  /// (the two cubits never share state directly, RNF06 — only
88	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen` bridges them).
89	  ///
90	  /// On success, persists every returned entry to the `entries` Hive box
91	  /// (`putAll`) *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return"
92	  /// ordering [list]/[getById] already use. Unlike [list]/[getById], there
93	  /// is no offline/timeout cache fallback here (AD-9: no client-side
94	  /// vector index) — every [Failure], including
95	  /// [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09).
96	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search(
97	    String query, {
98	    EntrySource? source,
99	    DateTime? dateFrom,
100	    DateTime? dateTo,
101	  });
102	}

27	/// The epic's ONE `GoRouter`/`redirect` (Boundaries: "never a second
28	/// competing `redirect`") — composes [VaultRepository.currentStatus] first,
29	/// then [SessionRepository.currentStatus] (AD-14). All three repositories
30	/// are taken as parameters (rather than this file reaching into `sl`
31	/// itself) purely so a test can pass fakes/mocks directly, without
32	/// touching the global DI container; `AccountSettingsRepository` (Story
33	/// 2.4) plays no part in `_redirect` and needs no `refreshListenable` entry
34	/// of its own — `currentBiometricEnabled` is read synchronously at
35	/// `/vault`'s own build time below, same convention `_redirect` already
36	/// uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`, so every fresh navigation into
37	/// `/vault` (triggered by those two streams, as already happens today)
38	/// already picks up the latest value correctly. (Review finding: a
39	/// `biometricEnabledStream` entry was tried here to also cover a value
40	/// changing while already resident at `/vault`, but go_router 18.1.1's
41	/// `GoRouterDelegate.setNewRoutePath` short-circuits whenever the matched
42	/// `RouteMatchList` is unchanged — which it always is here, since
43	/// `_redirect` stays at `/vault` before and after — so the route's
44	/// `builder` is never actually re-invoked that way; removed as dead code
45	/// rather than kept as a misleading no-op. That's a one-time, benign gap —
46	/// at most one extra biometric prompt on a slow-network cold boot, never a
47	/// security or dead-end issue, since PIN fallback is untouched and there's
48	/// no way to interrupt an in-flight native biometric dialog regardless —
49	/// which the frozen spec's I/O matrix never promised to cover.
50	/// `VaultLockScreen.didUpdateWidget` still defensively honors a changed
51	/// `attemptBiometricFirst` if the widget is ever rebuilt by some other
52	/// means.) The Configurações screen gets its own reactivity to this value
53	/// directly from `AccountSettingsCubit`'s independent subscription to
54	/// `biometricEnabledStream` — unrelated to routing.
55	///
56	/// [navigatorKey] is accepted explicitly (rather than letting `GoRouter`
57	/// generate its own internally) so the caller — `main.dart`'s
58	/// `ExpiryOverlayHost` — can reach the Navigator's own `BuildContext`
59	/// through the same, public, documented key instead of reaching into
60	/// `GoRouter`'s internal `routerDelegate` (not part of its public API).
61	GoRouter buildAppRouter({
62	  required VaultRepository vaultRepository,
63	  required SessionRepository sessionRepository,
64	  required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository,
65	  required GlobalKey<NavigatorState> navigatorKey,
66	}) {
67	  return GoRouter(
68	    navigatorKey: navigatorKey,
69	    initialLocation: AppRoutePaths.boot,
70	    refreshListenable: _GoRouterRefreshStream([
71	      vaultRepository.statusStream,
72	      sessionRepository.statusStream,
73	    ]),
74	    redirect: (context, state) =>
75	        _redirect(vaultRepository, sessionRepository, state),
76	    routes: [
77	      GoRoute(
78	        path: AppRoutePaths.vaultLock,
79	        builder: (context, state) => VaultLockScreen(
80	          vaultRepository: vaultRepository,
81	          // Story 2.4 — read synchronously, same sync-getter convention
82	          // `_redirect` already uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`
83	          // below: `true` (the default before the boot fetch resolves)
84	          // attempts biometric first, `false` skips straight to the PIN
85	          // keypad (Boundaries).
86	          attemptBiometricFirst:
87	              accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled,
88	        ),
89	      ),
90	      GoRoute(
91	        path: AppRoutePaths.boot,
92	        builder: (context, state) => const BootSplashScreen(),
93	      ),
94	      GoRoute(
95	        path: AppRoutePaths.auth,
96	        builder: (context, state) => AuthScreen(
97	          cubit: sl<AuthCubit>(),
98	          onAuthenticated: (context) => context.go(AppRoutePaths.home),
99	        ),
100	      ),
101	      GoRoute(
102	        path: AppRoutePaths.reauth,
103	        builder: (context, state) => const BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen(),
104	      ),
105	      GoRoute(
106	        path: AppRoutePaths.home,
107	        builder: (context, state) => const HomeChatPlaceholderScreen(),
108	      ),
109	      GoRoute(
110	        path: AppRoutePaths.meusRegistros,
111	        builder: (context, state) =>
112	            MeusRegistrosScreen(
113	              cubit: sl<MeusRegistrosCubit>(),
114	              searchCubit: sl<EntriesSearchCubit>(),
115	            ),
116	        routes: [
117	          // spec-4-4 (RF07) — `:id` is either a real server id or a
118	          // still-pending/failed placeholder's synthetic `tempId`
119	          // (Boundaries: "a valid, un-special-cased navigation target");
120	          // `EntryDetailCubit` itself decides nothing about which kind it
121	          // is, it just calls `getById` with it verbatim.
122	          GoRoute(
123	            path: ':id',
124	            builder: (context, state) => EntryDetailScreen(
125	              cubit: sl<EntryDetailCubit>()
126	                ..load(state.pathParameters['id']!),
127	            ),
128	          ),
129	        ],
130	      ),
131	      GoRoute(
132	        path: AppRoutePaths.planosDeAcao,
133	        builder: (context, state) => const ActionPlansPlaceholderScreen(),
134	      ),
135	      GoRoute(
136	        path: AppRoutePaths.configuracoes,
137	        builder: (context, state) =>
138	            AccountSettingsScreen(cubit: sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()),
139	      ),
140	    ],
141	  );
142	}
143	
144	/// I/O & Edge-Case Matrix:
145	/// - status not yet known (`null`) -> `/boot`, unless already there.
146	/// - `unauthenticated` -> `/auth`, unless already there.
147	/// - `authenticated`/`expired` -> leaves `/boot`/`/auth` for `/`; every
148	///   other location is left alone *except* `/reauth` while already
149	///   `authenticated` (bounced home below — `/reauth` is meant to be
150	///   reached only by the expiry overlay's own explicit navigation while
151	///   `expired`, code review Story 1.6) — a mid-session expiry never
152	///   navigates away (Story 1.5 behavior preserved), and the three
153	///   non-Home destinations stay reachable while `expired`.
154	///
155	/// AD-14: Epic 2's `VaultStatus` gate (RF03) is composed first, strictly
156	/// ahead of every `SessionStatus` check below — the vault gate overrides
157	/// any location whenever it isn't `unlocked`, and only once it is does the
158	/// rest of this function (unchanged from Story 1.6) ever run.
159	String? _redirect(
160	  VaultRepository vaultRepository,
161	  SessionRepository sessionRepository,
162	  GoRouterState state,
163	) {
164	  final location = state.matchedLocation;
165	
166	  // AD-14 — checked before SessionStatus, per Boundaries ("`_redirect`
167	  // checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`"). `VaultStatus.locked` is
168	  // the default from construction (never `null`), so this never waits on
169	  // an async warm-up the way the `status == null` boot check below does.
170	  if (vaultRepository.currentStatus != VaultStatus.unlocked) {
171	    return location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock ? null : AppRoutePaths.vaultLock;
172	  }
173	
174	  final status = sessionRepository.currentStatus;
175	
176	  if (status == null) {
177	    return location == AppRoutePaths.boot ? null : AppRoutePaths.boot;
178	  }
179	
180	  if (status == SessionStatus.unauthenticated) {
181	    return location == AppRoutePaths.auth ? null : AppRoutePaths.auth;
182	  }
183	
184	  // status is authenticated or expired.
185	  // `vaultLock` is included here too: once the vault unlocks while this
186	  // location is still `/vault` (the normal cold-start path once
187	  // `authenticate()` succeeds), the same fall-through that already bounces
188	  // `/boot`/`/auth` to Home applies — `/vault` is never a valid resting
189	  // place once `VaultStatus.unlocked`.
190	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.boot ||
191	      location == AppRoutePaths.auth ||
192	      location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock) {
193	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
194	  }
195	  // `/reauth` is a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's real
196	  // reauth flow; it should never be sitting open once the session is back
197	  // to fully `authenticated` (code review, Story 1.6).
198	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.reauth &&
199	      status == SessionStatus.authenticated) {
200	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
201	  }
202	  return null;
203	}
204	
205	/// Wraps [streams] as a single `Listenable` so `GoRouter`'s
206	/// `refreshListenable` can re-run [_redirect] on every emission from either
207	/// one — go_router 18.1.1 exports no `GoRouterRefreshStream` of its own
208	/// (Code Map), so this is that small local class. Extended by AD-14 to
209	/// subscribe to both the vault and the session streams (previously just
210	/// the one session stream), composing them into the one `Listenable`
211	/// `GoRouter` itself requires (Boundaries: "never a second
212	/// `GoRouter`/`redirect`").
213	class _GoRouterRefreshStream extends ChangeNotifier {
214	  _GoRouterRefreshStream(Iterable<Stream<dynamic>> streams) {
215	    _subscriptions = [
216	      for (final stream in streams)
217	        stream.listen(
218	          (_) => notifyListeners(),
219	          // Mirrors `ExpiryOverlayHost`'s and `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s own
220	          // subscriptions to this same stream — no current implementation
221	          // ever errors on it, but a future one that did must not surface
222	          // as an unhandled zone exception here specifically.
223	          onError: (_, _) {},
224	        ),
225	    ];
226	  }
227	
228	  late final List<StreamSubscription<dynamic>> _subscriptions;
229	
230	  @override
231	  void dispose() {
232	    for (final subscription in _subscriptions) {
233	      subscription.cancel();
234	    }
235	    super.dispose();
236	  }
237	}

1	/// `POST /entries`'s four possible origins (`openapi.yaml:345-351`). This
2	/// story only ever produces [manual] (Boundaries: "source=manual for this
3	/// story") — the other three exist here already so the port
4	/// ([EntriesRepository.create]) doesn't need to change shape when Stories
5	/// 3.2/3.3 (audio/photo) and RF10 (chat) start passing them.
6	enum EntrySource { manual, audio, photo, chat }
7	
8	/// A saved journal entry — plain `{id, content, source, chatMessageId,
9	/// occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt, mediaDurationSeconds}`
10	/// class, no `freezed` (mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`: this feature has no
11	/// need for the union/copyWith machinery `Failure` uses). Boundaries:
12	/// never a field beyond this exact set — `tags`/`piiStatus`/`piiSpans`/
13	/// `embeddingStatus` still belong to later epics, not this story.
14	/// [mediaDurationSeconds] was the one field Story 3.1 deferred (its own
15	/// comment named it "later epics") — spec-3-2 is that story, for the
16	/// `source: audio` entries it produces.
17	///
18	/// [occurredAt]/[createdAt]/[updatedAt] are kept as the backend's own ISO
19	/// 8601 strings rather than parsed into `DateTime` on this entity itself —
20	/// spec-4-1's `groupEntriesByDate()`/`EntryRecordCard`'s own time label
21	/// each parse [occurredAt] at their own call site instead, so a malformed
22	/// string only ever risks throwing at the one place that actually needs
23	/// the parsed value, never here.
24	class Entry {
25	  const Entry({
26	    required this.id,
27	    required this.content,
28	    required this.source,
29	    required this.chatMessageId,
30	    required this.occurredAt,
31	    required this.serverRevision,
32	    required this.createdAt,
33	    required this.updatedAt,
34	    this.mediaDurationSeconds,
35	  });
36	
37	  final String id;
38	  final String content;
39	  final EntrySource source;
40	
41	  /// Non-null only for a [EntrySource.chat]-sourced entry (RF10) — always
42	  /// `null` for this story's [EntrySource.manual] entries.
43	  final String? chatMessageId;
44	  final String occurredAt;
45	  final int serverRevision;
46	  final String createdAt;
47	  final String updatedAt;
48	
49	  /// Non-null only for an [EntrySource.audio]-sourced entry
50	  /// (`AudioEntryCubit.save()`) — `null` for every other source.
51	  final int? mediaDurationSeconds;
52	
53	  @override
54	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
55	      identical(this, other) ||
56	      (other is Entry &&
57	          other.id == id &&
58	          other.content == content &&
59	          other.source == source &&
60	          other.chatMessageId == chatMessageId &&
61	          other.occurredAt == occurredAt &&
62	          other.serverRevision == serverRevision &&
63	          other.createdAt == createdAt &&
64	          other.updatedAt == updatedAt &&
65	          other.mediaDurationSeconds == mediaDurationSeconds);
66	
67	  @override
68	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(
69	    id,
70	    content,
71	    source,
72	    chatMessageId,
73	    occurredAt,
74	    serverRevision,
75	    createdAt,
76	    updatedAt,
77	    mediaDurationSeconds,
78	  );
79	
80	  @override
81	  String toString() =>
82	      'Entry(id: $id, content: $content, source: $source, '
83	      'chatMessageId: $chatMessageId, occurredAt: $occurredAt, '
84	      'serverRevision: $serverRevision, createdAt: $createdAt, '
85	      'updatedAt: $updatedAt, '
86	      'mediaDurationSeconds: $mediaDurationSeconds)';
87	}

1	# Cerne — Prototype extract
2	
3	The visual reference of the product is `cerne-prototype.html` (this folder). Open it in a browser; it needs JavaScript. This extract lists its navigable states, its visual tokens, its components and the implementation notes that come with it.
4	
5	- **Frame:** 390 × 844 logical points, portrait only, 4 dp grid.
6	- **Language of the interface:** Portuguese. Every UI text below appears exactly as in the prototype, in quotes.
7	- **Precedence:** the prototype defines appearance and states. Behavior rules (triggers, timings, filters, error handling) are defined in `docs/input/requirements.md`; where the prototype's simulated behavior differs from a requirement, the requirement prevails.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Navigation map
12	
13	The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).
14	
15	```
16	Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
17	  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
18	  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
19	  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
20	  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
21	  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat
22	
23	Home/Chat (base screen)
24	  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
25	  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
26	  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
27	        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)
28	
29	Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
30	  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
31	  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
32	  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period
33	
34	Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)
35	
36	Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
37	  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
38	  ├─ inline profile-name editing
39	  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
40	  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
41	  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
42	```

46	## 2. Navigable states
47	
48	Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.
49	
50	### 2.1 Entry and authentication
51	| State | What it shows |
52	|---|---|
53	| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
54	| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
55	| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
56	| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
57	| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
58	| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |
59	
60	### 2.2 Conversation
61	| State | What it shows |
62	|---|---|
63	| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
64	| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
65	| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
66	| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
67	| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
68	| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
69	| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
70	| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |

73	Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.

81	| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |

7	/// One message bubble — user (Boundaries: `colorChatBubbleUser`, squared
8	/// bottom-right corner) vs AI (`colorSurfaceElevated`, squared bottom-left
9	/// corner, resting [DesignTokens.elevation1]). Exactly the 3 visible
10	/// states RF04's Acceptance Criteria names render here, driven by
11	/// [ChatUiMessage.status]: `streaming` (progressive text + blinking
12	/// cursor), `failed` (a generic error indicator replaces the timestamp
13	/// slot — never the tap-to-retry copy, Boundaries: "generic error
14	/// indicator (not retry copy)" — Story 6.3's job), `complete` (plain
15	/// text, nothing else). [ChatUiMessage.content] itself is rendered as-is
16	/// in every state — never cleared on failure (I/O matrix).
17	class ChatBubble extends StatefulWidget {
18	  const ChatBubble({required this.message, super.key});
19	
20	  final ChatUiMessage message;
21	
22	  @override
23	  State<ChatBubble> createState() => _ChatBubbleState();
24	}

26	class _ChatBubbleState extends State<ChatBubble>
27	    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
28	  late final AnimationController _cursorController;
29	
30	  @override
31	  void initState() {
32	    super.initState();
33	    _cursorController = AnimationController(
34	      vsync: this,
35	      duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 600),
36	    );
37	    _syncCursorAnimation();
38	  }
39	
40	  @override
41	  void didUpdateWidget(ChatBubble oldWidget) {
42	    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
43	    _syncCursorAnimation();
44	  }

47	  /// that finalizes to `complete`/`failed` must stop ticking forever
48	  /// after, both so a long-lived chat session never leaks one live
49	  /// `AnimationController` per past message, and so nothing waiting on
50	  /// "every animation in the tree has settled" (e.g. a test's own
51	  /// `pumpAndSettle()`) ever blocks on a bubble that finished streaming.
52	  void _syncCursorAnimation() {
53	    final shouldAnimate = widget.message.status == ChatMessageStatus.streaming;
54	    if (shouldAnimate && !_cursorController.isAnimating) {
55	      _cursorController.repeat(reverse: true);
56	    } else if (!shouldAnimate && _cursorController.isAnimating) {
57	      _cursorController.stop();

121	                color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,

Implemented spec-6-1 (Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response) in full, per the spec's own frozen Intent/Boundaries/I-O matrix. All context files listed in the spec's frontmatter plus every file in its Code Map were read before writing any code.

## What was built

**`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`** — added `postStream()` (`ResponseType.stream`, reusing `_mapDioException`) and a dedicated `_mapStreamDioException()` helper. Found and fixed a real correctness gap along the way: dio never auto-decodes a stream-typed response's error body into a `Map`, even on a non-2xx status (it hands back the raw, undrained `ResponseBody`), so a real backend error on `chat-messages-send` would otherwise always collapse to `Failure.malformedResponse` regardless of its actual code. `_mapStreamDioException` drains and JSON-decodes that body once, falling back to the generic mapping on any decode failure.

**`lib/features/chat/`** — full vertical slice:
- `domain/entities`: `ChatSession`, `ChatMessage` (role/status enums), sealed `ChatStreamEvent` (`ChatMessageCreatedEvent`/`ChatTokenEvent`/`ChatDoneEvent`). No Flutter import, no `data/` import (RNF06 — verified by grep).
- `domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`: abstract `ChatRepository` — `Future<Either<Failure,T>>` for everything except `sendMessage`, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>` (RNF09).
- `data/models`: `ChatSessionDto`/`ChatMessageDto` (`json_serializable`, generated `.g.dart` via `build_runner`, zero conflicts) with `toEntity()`.
- `data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart`: non-streaming calls via `ApiClient`'s JSON methods; `sendMessage()` owns the SSE line-splitting (buffers across chunk boundaries, parses `event:`/`data:` blocks, discards `context`, maps `done`/`error`/`token`/`message_created`, skips unknown event names, maps any parse failure to `malformedResponse`, and emits a trailing `Left(NetworkTimeout)` if the connection ends with no terminal event).
- `data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`: Hive-backed cache fallback (`chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` boxes) for `listSessions`/`listMessages` on offline/timeout only; `createSession`/`sendMessage` have no fallback (blocked offline / no write queue, per spec).
- `chat_injection.dart` + `injection_container.dart`: `registerChatFeature()` wired in after `registerCaptureFeature()`.
- `presentation/cubit`: sealed `ChatState` (`ChatBootstrapLoading`/`ChatBootstrapError`/`ChatReady`), `ChatCubit.init()` (list-or-create session, no-op once already `ChatReady`) and `.sendMessage()` (optimistic bubbles, token-by-token append, finalize/fail by id, guards against a concurrent second send, text never cleared on failure).
- `presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart` + `presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`: real screen reusing the former placeholder's header/drawer chrome, composer with "+" → `InsertionModal.show` unchanged, 3 visible bubble states.

**Navigation**: `app_router.dart` now builds `ChatScreen(cubit: sl<ChatCubit>())` at `/`; `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` (and its now-dead `_FeaturePlaceholderBody` helper) deleted from `placeholder_screens.dart`. Stale doc-comment mentions fixed in `app_drawer.dart` and `entry_record_card.dart`.

**Design tokens**: added `chatBubbleMaxWidthFraction`, `chatBubblePadding`, `chatBubbleGap`, `chatFailureIndicatorPadding` to `design_tokens.dart` (prototype-extract.md is silent on bubble sizing; decided and documented per AGENTS.md policy) — RNF08 holds, zero new hardcoded visual values elsewhere.

**Tests updated**: `app_router_test.dart`, `main_test.dart`, `placeholder_screens_test.dart` — swapped every `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` assertion to `ChatScreen`, added a fake-`ChatRepository`-backed `ChatCubit` DI override in each (mirroring the existing `MeusRegistrosCubit`/`VaultRepository` fake-swap pattern), dropped the placeholder's own test group and its now-dead fakes/imports.

**New tests** (51 total, all passing): `api_client_test.dart` (+6, covering `postStream` incl. the stream-error-body decode fix), `test/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source_test.dart` (12, full SSE matrix: happy path, cross-chunk buffering, mid-stream drop, in-band error, offline, malformed payload, unknown event), `.../data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart` (9, cache fallback behavior), `.../presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` (12, bootstrap + all 3 message states + concurrent-send guard), `.../presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart` (6, visual states + Reduce Motion), `.../presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` (6, end-to-end screen wiring incl. "+" opening `InsertionModal`).

One real bug caught by this last test pass and fixed: `ChatBubble`'s cursor `AnimationController` was calling `..repeat(reverse: true)` unconditionally in `initState`, so it never stopped ticking even after a message finished streaming — this hung `pumpAndSettle()` in any test touching a post-stream screen and would have quietly leaked a live ticker per historical message in production. Fixed with a `_syncCursorAnimation()` guard (start/stop keyed off `status == streaming`) called from `initState`/`didUpdateWidget`.

## Verification

- `fvm flutter analyze`: **0 issues**.
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs`: regenerated the two new DTOs' `.g.dart`, 0 conflicts, idempotent on rerun.
- `fvm flutter test`: **889/889 passing** (838 pre-existing + 51 new; zero regressions).

## Left incomplete / risks worth flagging

- RNF07's ≥80% domain-coverage target was not measured with a coverage tool (not in the spec's own Verification command list); the new domain layer is small and plain-value, so risk is low, but it's unverified.
- `ChatCubit`'s concurrent-send guard (ignore `sendMessage()` while a bubble is already `streaming`) is my own addition to stand in for 6.3's real offline/composer lock, per the spec's Boundaries ("Ask First: none identified... to avoid colliding with 6.2"); it's documented in the cubit's own doc comment as intentionally minimal.
- The `_mapStreamDioException` fix (decoding a stream-typed error response body) is a behavior improvement beyond the literal task list ("reusing `_mapDioException`") — scoped deliberately to `ApiClient.postStream` only, not touched in `dio_error_code.dart`/`RetryInterceptor`, so a retryable code returned as an HTTP error status on `chat-messages-send` still won't be auto-retried by `RetryInterceptor` (it only sees `Map`-shaped bodies); it will, however, now surface as the *correct* `Failure` subtype to the UI instead of `malformedResponse`.
- No device/simulator exists yet (per AGENTS.md), so this was verified only via `flutter test`/`flutter analyze`, not a real device run against the real backend.

Key files (all absolute paths under `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b`): `lib/core/network/api_client.dart`, `lib/features/chat/**`, `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart`, `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart`, `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`, `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart`, `test/features/chat/**`, `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart`, `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/core/navigation/placeholder_screens_test.dart`, `test/main_test.dart`.
